prerequisites: Basic knowledge of technical mechanics, especially from the preceding modules Mechanics 1 and Mechanics 2.

learning_outcomes.text: Explain and apply analytical methods of mechanics such as the principle of virtual work.
Set up Lagrangian equations of motion for systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom and analyze small oscillations around equilibrium positions.
Describe large deformations and stress states of a classical continuum.
Explain and apply relationships of linearized elasticity theory.
Explain the classical theorems of linearized elasticity theory.
Apply the fundamentals of elasticity theory to straight beams.
Analyze statically indeterminate beam systems using the force method and Castigliano's principle.
Analyze stability and vibrations of beams.
Formulate Ritz approaches for beam constructions and calculate approximate solutions using them.
Analyze complex problems in a structured manner.
Present own calculation methods and solutions appropriately to the target audience.

syllabus_topics: Hamilton's principle and Lagrangian equations of the first and second kind
Lyapunov's concept of stability; stability analysis of equilibrium positions
Fundamentals of continuum mechanics (strain tensor, stress tensor, material equations)
